derivation: probably from a primary verb (to join);
def: peace (literally or figuratively); by implication, prosperity
kjv: one, peace, quietness, rest, + set at one again

occurrences.text: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.
Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.
And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.
Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word:
And into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house.
And if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it: if not, it shall turn to you again.
Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:
Saying, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.
And as they thus spake, Jesus himself stood in the midst of them, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.

These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you.
And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.
And the next day he shewed himself unto them as they strove, and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, ye are brethren; why do ye wrong one to another?
Then had the churches rest throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified; and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied.
The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)

And after they had tarried there a space, they were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles.

To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile:
And the way of peace have they not known:
Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!
For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.
Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another.
Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.

Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ,
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Those things, which ye have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, do: and the God of peace shall be with you.

And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.

To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.
Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
